newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Autopsy on Menem's son shows no evidence of murder.
newsitem.headline: Autopsy on Menem's son shows no evidence of murder.

text.p: An autopsy on the son of Argentine President Carlos Menem more than a year after he died in a helicopter crash turned up no evidence he was murdered or on drugs, a federal judge said on Monday.

The autopsy, ordered after Carlos Menem Jr.'s mother suspected foul play, proved the 26-year old died from multiple fractures to his skull and other bones in his body, judge Carlos Villafuerte told Reuters.
"It concludes his death was caused by multiple fractures to the cranium and other bones," Villafuerte said. "There was no evidence of any toxic substance or drugs."

Menem's ex-wife, Zulema Yoma, suspecting her son was murdered and accusing Menem of covering up information, convinced the judge to exhume the body last July. She has suggested her son was the victim of dirty politics or drug trafficking.
Media reports, denied by authorities, have suggested that Menem Jr. may have been shot or that he had consumed drugs or alcohol before the crash.
Government officials have insisted that Carlos Jr. died when the helicopter he was piloting accidentally hit a power line and crashed in March 1995.
The president said the crash was an accident and that Zulema's suffering as a bereaved mother fuelled her suspicions. But he agreed to the autopsy.
Villafuerte said the autopsy was not enough to determine that Carlos Jr.'s death was accidental.
Perhaps more important will be the results of an ongoing study of the fragments of the helicopter he was piloting, Villafueerte said.
The autopsy was not conducted earlier because the physicians who examined the body of Carlos Jr. after the crash thought the cause was evident.
Menem and Yoma, both of Syrian origin, had a stormy high-profile marriage which ended when Menem locked her out of the presidential residence soon after taking office in 1989.
